findings.spec: FR-7: the message includes the Google review link through our redirect, which counts clicks; Flow 2 step 3
findings.summary: A send whose outcome is unknown (timeout, lost connection, ambiguous 5xx) is marked failed with outcome_unknown and sent_at cleared, but may have reached the customer. recordClick and reviewLinkFor required sent_at, so that customer's link returned 404 instead of the review form.
findings.verification: new tests in src/requests/requests.test.ts fail on main f3d6d49 and at 3166329 (worktree), pass with the fix
findings.fix: redirect accepts sent_at not null OR (status failed AND outcome_unknown)

findings.summary: askedRecently dates an outcome-unknown failure by scheduled_for because sent_at is cleared. A request held while its business was not live can go out up to 72 hours after scheduled_for, so its 90-day window can end up to 3 days early. Recommend keeping the attempt time (for example a separate attempted_at) if exact windows matter.

sendDueRequests catches errors per row only before the claim. If the failure-path transaction in deliver() throws (database error after a provider error), the whole run throws, the row stays sent with no failed record, and the rest of the batch waits for the queue retry. Not a double send; rare.

findings.status: documented (owner to decide; SPEC not edited)
findings.summary: sms_opt_ins rows hold a phone number and are kept indefinitely: retention (12 months after the last visit) covers customer rows only and #57 keeps opt-in rows on purpose. Decide how long consent evidence is kept (TCPA record-keeping vs minimum data) and add it to the Data model and privacy pages. A lawyer should check the period.
Same question as A-45-1 from the retention side; #57's PR raises it. Recorded once as A-45-1.

Implementation status FR-23 still says the support address is a placeholder (hello@kindword.example); #48 set CONTACT_EMAIL to hello@kindword.fun. src/compliance/compliance.ts still calls it a placeholder in a comment. Next SPEC sync should update the row (Doc and docs/SPEC.md).

findings.classification: latent bug (not reproducible yet: FR-15 not built)
findings.summary: The monthly report counts replies posted from reply_drafts.posted_at. Drafts are purged with their review within 30 days (FR-22, purge at 29 days), so a reply posted early in a month can be gone before the report on the 1st. The Data model says own metrics survive the purge through the audit log (as approvals already do). Recommend FR-15 (#49) write a posted audit row and the report count those.

Link clicks in the report can exceed requests sent: a click on an outcome-unknown send (now possible with #60) counts as a click but the send does not count as sent. Acceptable (real click); noted for reading the figures.
operatorAlerts.sendFailures also runs NOT EXISTS on audit_log by entity/entity_id/action, which has no index. Fine at pilot scale.

observations: #43: refused = !retryable || 429 in both adapters; only outcome_unknown counts toward FR-9; DB check keeps outcome_unknown only on failed rows; migration 0010 additive.

#45: opt-in box unchecked, consent statement names the business, number, not-a-condition, frequency, rates, HELP/STOP; rows only on checked box and valid number; no logging; 404 once offboarded; migration 0011 additive with phone and wording checks.
#46: per-row catch rolls back only that row; bad zones sorted last in all three scans.
#44: handleCallback retry option matches @vercel/queue 0.11 types; maxDeliveries 6 in vercel.json equals MAX_DELIVERIES; config errors are not retried; logs carry counts and codes only.
#53: figures from Google kept in memory only; audit row holds month only; no review text, names or reply text in the email; idempotent (lock, audit row, key).
#54: no personal data in the alert email; each failure, token failure and stale period alerted once; offboarded businesses excluded, matching poll.ts.
#57: importer and purge share the per-location lock and the same cutoff (<=); suppression rows kept; cascade removes visits and requests.
#52: assertions narrowed to the fields that can carry personal data; not weakened.
